info.title: mfgopredict service
info.description: GO molecular-function prediction for free-text protein function labels. Also an MCP server at /mcp (Streamable HTTP), one tool per endpoint.

get.description: Liveness, and whether the KEGG KO table is loaded (`ko_loaded`, `ko_terms`).

Versions, available embedding models, CUDA/NVML status, cost rates,
measured throughput, loaded predictors, and whether the CONCORDIA council can run.

Live state of every GPU NVML can see, for dashboards.

Always 200: without NVML the body says `available: false` and why.
`processes=false` skips the per-process listing (cheaper, and it hides
other users' command lines).

post.description:
Predict GO molecular-function (GO-MF) terms for protein function labels.

`labels`: free-text labels as annotation tools write them (RAST roles,
Bakta/Prokka products, "EC 2.7.1.31", KEGG KO ids, prose). `ids`, if
given, is parallel to `labels` and echoed back. No LLM is involved.

Returns `predictions`: one row per candidate term, `rank` 1 first, with
`id`, `label`, `go_id`, `go_name`, `band` (HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW),
`score` (measured precision lower bound of the evidence path, so the
same for every row with the same `how`), `how` (evidence path, e.g.
`text:ec->go`, `layer1`) and `is_alternate` (rank > 1: a competing
reading, not a second function). `band` grades rank 1; alternates are
always LOW. Layer-1 rows also carry `cosine`, the per-candidate
similarity, and `surface`, the GO name or synonym it matched. A label
naming several functions ("X / Y") is split, and `part` names the part.
`topk` sets how many candidates come back per part (default 5, at most
50); `top1: true` keeps rank 1 only. `status` has one row per label saying whether it was attempted and
predicted; a label with no prediction appears only there. Also `counts`
and `cost` (GPU time and price, when `use_gpu`).

mixed.summary: One of each label kind (EC, name, split, hypothetical)
mixed.description: g1 names one EC number: `text:ec->go`, plus a looser name match as an alternate. g2 names two EC numbers: two rank-1/rank-2 terms (`set_shape: antichain`). g3 matches a GO name exactly (`text:name->go:exact`, band HIGH). g4 names two functions, so it is split and each prediction carries `part`. g5 is not attempted: it appears only in `status`.

minimal.description: Everything else takes its default; `id` comes back as the index, "0".

candidates.description: topk=10 returns the 10 nearest GO terms by Layer-1 cosine, rank 1 first; compare their `cosine` values to see how close the runners-up are. Changing topk reuses the loaded model.

layer0_only.summary: Layer 0 only: lookups, no model, no GPU
layer0_only.description: use_layer1=false answers from EC, KEGG KO and GO-name lookups only. Fast and needs no embedding model, but free text with no EC number or exact name (row 2) gets no prediction.

top1.description: top1=true drops the alternates (`is_alternate: true`), leaving one row per label, or per part for a split label.

kegg_ko.description: A bare KO id routes to the KO table (`how: ko:kegg_go` or `ko:ec->go`). Needs MFGOPREDICT_KO set on the server; GET /health says `ko_loaded`. Without it the label is attempted but not predicted.

gpu.summary: Layer 1 on a GPU, with a stricter band cut
gpu.description: use_gpu=true runs the Layer-1 embedding on GPU `gpu_index` (as in GET /gpu); `cost` then reports GPU time and price. tau raises the cosine below which a Layer-1 match is banded LOW. POST /estimate with the same body projects the cost first.

post.description:
Project the GPU cost of a /predict call with the same body, without running it.

Triage and Layer 0 run for real on the CPU; that is how the Layer-1 workload
is known exactly. Only the encode time is projected, from measured
throughput.

Whether POST /concordia_go_council can run here, and if not, why. Always 200.

`available` and `reason`; the `default_roster` (which model sits in each
seat), the named `profiles` a request can pick, and `missing_credentials`
for any seat without an API key. `auth.key_configured` says whether the
POST can be authorised at all (it needs the `X-API-Key` header).

post.description:
Assign GO molecular-function (GO-MF) terms to protein annotation strings,
using mfgopredict to find candidate terms and a council of LLMs to choose among them.

**Input.** `items`: 1 to 20 annotation strings, as a genome annotation tool
wrote them, each `{"text": "..."}`. Everything else is optional:

- per item: `id` (echoed back), `source` (the tool that wrote the text, e.g.
  `RAST_annotation`, `prokka`, `bakta`; the models see it), `gene_id` (rows
  with the same gene share candidate terms), `candidates` (your own menu of
  GO terms, which replaces step 2 below);
- request-wide: `force_council`, `profile` / `roles` (which models sit in
  which seat), and the menu settings `retrieval_k`, `cap`, `max_height`,
  `use_layer1`, `use_gpu`, `pool_by_gene`. The defaults suit normal use.

Minimal body: `{"items": [{"text": "Glycerate kinase (EC 2.7.1.31)"}]}`

**What happens to each item.** mfgopredict runs on every item:

1. mfgopredict triages the text. A text that states no function (a bare
   gene symbol like `glxK`, a COG/Pfam/TIGR/InterPro id, a locus tag,
   "hypothetical protein") stops here: `decided_by: "guard"`, no terms.
2. mfgopredict builds a closed menu of up to `cap` (40) candidate GO-MF
   terms: terms mapped from EC numbers in the text first, then GO name and
   synonym matches, then Layer-1 embedding retrieval (unless
   `use_layer1: false`). Its own ranked predictions are kept too.
3. If every candidate came from an exact EC or exact name match and they
   make one answer, mfgopredict's term is returned without any model call:
   `decided_by: "mfgopredict"`. `force_council: true` sends it to the
   council anyway.
4. Otherwise three proposer models each pick terms from the menu, a critic
   audits the vote, and a meta reviewer settles disagreements:
   `decided_by: "council"`. The council can only pick terms on the menu.
   If the menu is empty: `decided_by: "menu"`, no terms.

**Output.** `items` has one row per input item, in input order. Read
`final_go_ids` (a list of `{go_id, name}`; more than one means a
multifunctional protein and all apply) and `status`. An empty
`final_go_ids` with `status: "ok"` is a decline, and `decline_reason`
says why: `contentless` (the text states no function),
`no_candidate_matched` (it does, but no menu term fits) or
`no_candidates` (empty menu). `status: "error"` means a model call failed:
retry the item, it is not a "no term" answer. Each row also carries the
`menu` offered, mfgopredict's own predictions (`mfgopredict`) and, for
council rows, every seat's vote and reasoning (`council`). Top-level
`counts` tallies rows by `decided_by`; `usage` counts model calls and tokens.

**Auth.** Needs the council API key in the `X-API-Key` header (it spends
LLM API money): 401 without it or with a wrong one, 503 if this server
has no key configured. Every other endpoint is open.

**Cost and errors.** A council row takes about 10 to 30 s; guard and
mfgopredict rows take milliseconds. Replies are cached, so repeating a
request is cheap. 503 when the council cannot run here (no CONCORDIA
checkout on its dev branch, no `openai` package, or no API key for a seat);
GET /concordia_go_council says which. 422 for a bad body or roster.

mixed.summary: One of each outcome (council, mfgopredict, guard)
mixed.description: Row 1 has two EC numbers, so two EC terms and the council picks. Row 2 has one exact EC match, so mfgopredict answers with no model call. Row 3 is a bare gene symbol, so the guard declines it. Row 4 has no EC number; its menu comes from Layer-1 retrieval and the council picks.

one_gene_many_tools.summary: Several tools' annotations of the same gene, pooled
one_gene_many_tools.description: All three rows share gene_id `fig|83333.1.peg.1234`, so each row's menu also gets the other rows' terms (marked `pooled_from`). The prokka and bakta rows have no EC number, but they are offered both EC terms the RAST row found.

force_council.summary: Make the council judge rows mfgopredict would answer alone
force_council.description: Both rows have a single exact EC match, which normally skips the council. force_council=true sends them anyway, e.g. to compare the two.

own_menu.summary: Bring your own candidate GO terms
own_menu.description: `candidates` replaces the menu builder: the council may only pick from these three terms. `score` is required for origin `retrieval`.

swap_a_seat.summary: Change which model sits in a seat
swap_a_seat.description: `roles` overrides seats on top of the profile (the default roster is proposers gemini35flash, gpt54, gpt55; critic claudesonnet5; meta claudeopus45). A model may hold only one seat. `profile` picks a named roster from the council config; GET /concordia_go_council lists them.

cheap_menu.summary: Tune the menu: smaller, Layer 0 only, or on a GPU
cheap_menu.description: use_layer1=false builds the menu from EC and name matches only (no embedding model), so free text without an EC number gets no menu (`decided_by: menu`). Set use_gpu=true instead to run Layer 1 faster.

get.description:
Model aliases a council seat can take (`roles` / profiles), paid vs free. Always 200.

Asks every configured endpoint what it serves right now (`GET /models`).
- `paid`: Argo models. Every call is billed per token.
- `free`: models on your own OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, Ollama, the
  model_service containers), registered in model_inference.yaml. No
  per-call cost; they use your GPU.
Each entry: `alias` (put this in `roles`), `name`, `endpoint`, `owned_by`,
`status`, `online` (= status is `available`) and `seats`
(`<profile>:<role>` wherever it already sits). Free entries also carry
`url` (as this service reaches it), `public_url` and `port` (as a browser
reaches it, host from $VLLM_PUBLIC_HOST), `gpus` (where it is loaded) and
`detail` (why it is not available, and how to fix it).
`status`: `available` (loaded, answering); `starting` (loading weights);
`stopping`; `stopped` (container up, model not loaded: POST
<service>/service/start?gpus=<index>); `failed` (vLLM crashed or refused
the GPU, see `detail`); `not_served` (server up, model not in its list);
`not_running` (nothing listening: container or server down);
`unresponsive` (something listens but did not answer in 3 s).
`unconfigured`: served by an OSS server but not named in the council config,
so not usable yet (an unknown alias goes to Argo). `unknown_seats`: aliases a
roster uses that no endpoint serves. `endpoints`: reachability, `port`,
`public_base_url` and `public_control_url` (the model_service /service/*
root) per endpoint.

Models the AmSC MAG (American Science Cloud Model Access Gateway) serves
to your AmSC token.

**Auth.** Your own AmSC access token as the `X-AmSC-Token` header (or
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). Which models you see depends on the
token's AmSC project. Without one, the server's
`MFGOPREDICT_SERVICE_AMSC_MAG_TOKEN` is used if set; otherwise 401.

Returns `gateway` (the base URL, OpenAI-compatible at `<gateway>/v1`),
`count`, `providers` (models per provider) and `models`: the gateway's
entries (`id`, `owned_by`, and where it reports them `mode`,
`max_input_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`), each with `provider`, the part of
the id after `@`. Errors: 401/403 when the gateway rejects the token, 502
when it is unreachable or answers oddly, 504 when it is too slow.

post.description:
mfgopredict's side of the council for each item: guard, candidate menu and
deterministic answer. No LLM call, no API key.

Per item: `triage_class`; `guard` (why the text states no function, else
null: such rows get no terms and skip the council); `deterministic` (an
exact EC or name match answers alone: `{go_id, name, band, how}`, else null);
`menu` (the closed menu, already in the `candidates` format the stage
endpoints take); `mfgopredict` (its own top 5, for comparison). Council rows
are those with no `guard`, no `deterministic` and a non-empty `menu`.

To judge a candidate list you already have (e.g. POST /predict's ranked
terms), skip this endpoint and send it as `candidates` to the stages; see
docs/concordia-staged.md.

council_menu.description: EC terms, then name matches, then Layer-1 retrieval, capped at `cap`.

post.description:
One proposer model over many items: which menu terms each annotation supports.

Send `model` and `items` (`text`, `source`, `candidates`). Returns per item
`proposal`: `{picked: [{go_id, confidence, why}], overall_confidence,
no_functional_content, notes}`, or `{error}` with `status: "error"`.
Picks off the menu are dropped. Collect each proposer model's `proposal`
into the next stage's `proposers: [{model, proposal}, ...]`.
Needs `X-API-Key`; 503 when the model is not loaded.

One critic model over many items: audits the proposers' vote.

Each item adds `proposers` (ordered `[{model, proposal}]`). Returns per item
`critic`: `{verdict, reason, overpicked, missed, contentless_input}` or
`{error}`, and the vote it saw: `votes` (go_id -> count) and `n_valid`.

One meta-reviewer model over many items: the final call from the proposers
and the critic. Always calls the model (the council's skip rule is in
POST /concordia/go/assemble).

Each item adds `critic`. Returns per item `meta`: `{final_go_ids,
final_confidence, no_functional_content, reasoning, skipped: false}` or
`{error, final_go_ids: []}`. `final_go_ids` keeps menu terms only.

The council's decision from its stages' outputs, exactly as
POST /concordia_go_council makes it. No LLM call, no API key.

Per item send `proposers`, `critic` and, on the second pass, `meta`.
Returns `needs_meta: true` when the council would ask the meta reviewer
(the proposers disagree or the critic objected): call POST /concordia/go/meta
for that row, then assemble again with `meta`. Otherwise the final record:
`status` (`error` if any stage failed), `decline_reason`, `final_go_ids`,
`final_confidence`, `votes`, `n_valid` and `meta` (the skip record when the
council agreed; a `meta` sent for such a row is ignored, as the council
would not have asked).

model.description: The one model alias this stage calls (GET /models)

proposers.title: Proposers
proposers.description: Distinct model aliases that vote, e.g. [gemini35flash, gpt54, gpt55]

critic.title: Critic
critic.description: Model alias that audits the vote, e.g. claudesonnet5

meta.title: Meta
meta.description: Model alias that settles disagreements, e.g. claudeopus45

RoleOverride.title: RoleOverride
RoleOverride.description: Seats to replace; unset ones keep the profile's model.

Roster.title: Roster
Roster.description: Who sits where. Checked here because CONCORDIA only checks it in main().

id.title: Id
id.description: Your id for this row, echoed back; unset = its index

source.title: Source
source.description: Shown to the model as "Produced by: …"

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description: The closed menu, e.g. `menu` from POST /concordia/go/menu. Send the same menu, in the same order, to every stage of one item

AmSCToken.description: Your AmSC access token (a JWT from identity.amsc.ornl.gov)
AmSCToken.name: X-AmSC-Token

APIKeyHeader.description: Council API key, set when the image was built
APIKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
